Architecture

Persistence, schema and migrations

PostgreSQL stores records; UE Actors hold short-lived session projections.

On this page
Minimal development setupModel contractSave semanticsMigration procedure

Minimal development setup

Use one PostgreSQL18 instance and one GameService app. Create a game runtime database role with only required data permissions and a separate migration/backup operator role. Clients never receive SQL connection strings. Local development authentication fixtures cannot be enabled by a production client option.

Start with identity/character/appearance and idempotent creation in Phase04, expand base item/stack/wallet/session/receipt/schema records in05 before rewards08. Inventory presentation arrives09, but stable item identity and transactional reward contracts cannot wait until after kill rewards exist.

Model contract

Database model pages enumerate keys, integer bounds, row versions, references and transaction paths. Use UUIDs for nonstackable instances and stable definition IDs for immutable templates. Keep quantities and currency as bounded integers. Canonical currency is one base integer; copper/silver/gold are display formatting, never three contradictory balances.

ReadCommitted with explicit row locking is the initial transaction strategy for known character/container/source rows. Evaluate Serializable for operations whose invariants span predicates; it requires complete-transaction retry on serialization failures. Merely selecting a stronger isolation name does not remove application validation or capacity constraints.

Save semantics

A accepted durable command is committed before its success is displayed. Ordinary movement may checkpoint periodically under a documented loss window, while high-value economic state is immediately durable. A zone runtime cache cannot silently claim durability for a failed write. Long-lived cooldown/recovery snapshots prevent reconnect from resetting important gates; short combat effects may clear under the documented recovery policy.

Logout marks the session draining, cancels unresolved actions, settles accepted transactions and writes the current safe location/version. Crash recovery reconstructs latest committed character facts; uncommitted fishing/crafting progress follows explicit cancel/status policies, not rollback of inventory to an old disk snapshot.

Migration procedure

  1. Write a numbered migration with exact table/constraint changes, expected old version and invariant assertions.
  2. Restore a backup to disposable staging; run migration, then old/new record decode tests and the economic route.
  3. Run again: already-applied migration does not duplicate rows or rewards. Inject interruption and test the recovery plan.
  4. For incompatible patches drain admissions, settle commands, apply tested migration and deploy compatible service/zone/client catalogs.
  5. Retain backup metadata and a tested forward-fix/restore decision. Do not promise every schema change has a safe automatic reverse migration.
